candidate_title: A Survey of Neural Translation Methods and Research Resources
candidate_abstract: Machine translation uses computers to translate between human languages and is a major application of natural language processing. candidate_title: Testing How Well Structural Knowledge Prompts Generalize
candidate_abstract: Large language models generate text well but can produce factual errors. Structural knowledge prompting supplies external knowledge through structured representations and has achieved leading results on knowledge-intensive tasks. Most evaluations concentrate on individual problems, leaving the limits of this approach unclear. We examine granularity, transferability, scalability and universality through SUBARU, a new benchmark with nine tasks that vary in difficulty and the level of structure they address.

candidate_abstract: We give a mathematical account of the actor objective in soft actor-critic, tracing the derivation from its theoretical form to the loss used in implementations. candidate_title: Using Reinforcement Learning to Choose Approximate Computing Designs
candidate_abstract: Approximate computing can improve application performance at the cost of accuracy. Choosing a suitable approximation for a given application remains difficult. We use reinforcement learning to search for designs that balance three objectives: accuracy loss, power use and computation time. On some benchmarks, the selected approximations reduced power use and execution time with a favorable accuracy trade-off.
